subjects.title: Foundation Course in GIS and Remote Sensing

units.title: Introduction to Remote Sensing
units.topics: Definition and scope of remote sensing (RS), Historical development of remote sensing technology, Basic principles and concepts: Energy source and radiation, Interaction with atmosphere and surface, Data acquisition and interpretation, Applications of remote sensing in: Agriculture, forestry, water resources, Urban planning, disaster management, Environmental monitoring and biodiversity

units.title: Electromagnetic Spectrum in Remote Sensing
units.topics: Overview of the Electromagnetic Spectrum (EMS), Important spectral regions used in RS Visible, Infrared (Near, Mid, Thermal), Microwave, Spectral signatures and reflectance characteristics, Atmospheric windows and their relevance in RS

units.title: Platforms and Sensors
units.topics: Classification of remote sensing platforms: Ground-based, Airborne (Aircraft, UAVs/Drones), Spaceborne (Satellites); Sensor types and characteristics: Spatial, spectral, temporal, and radiometric resolution; Types of sensors: Optical, Thermal, Microwave, Multispectral, Hyperspectral; Overview of major remote sensing satellites and missions (e.g., Landsat, Sentinel, IRS)

units.title: Types of Remote Sensing
units.topics: Passive Remote Sensing: Concept and working principle, Sun as energy source, Examples: Optical and thermal sensors; Active Remote Sensing: Concept and working principle: Artificial energy sources (microwave/laser), Comparison: Passive vs Active RS (advantages and limitations); Overview of: Radar (Radio Detection and Ranging), Lidar (Light Detection and Ranging)

units.title: Remote Sensing – Practical
units.topics: Introduction to Satellite Image Interpretation: Introduction to Google Earth as a visualization tool, Understanding geographical coordinates (Latitude/Longitude), Identifying major landforms and features using satellite imagery; Visual interpretation techniques: Shape, size, tone, texture, pattern, shadow, and association, Urban vs. Rural features, vegetation vs. water bodies; Overview of satellite data sources and portals; Hands-on exercise: USGS Earth Explorer, Copernicus Open Access Hub

units.title: Fundamentals of GIS
units.topics: Definition and scope of GIS, Spatial and non-spatial data, Layers, features, and attributes; Components of GIS: Hardware, software, data, people, and methods; GIS Data Models: Raster model, Vector model; Coordinate Systems: GCS vs PCS, Common coordinate systems (WGS 84, UTM); Map Projections: Concept and necessity, Examples (Mercator, Lambert, UTM); Georeferencing: Definition and importance, Techniques to align maps/images with real-world coordinates

units.title: Practical in GIS
units.topics: Introduction to QGIS: Installation and interface navigation, project files, toolbars, panels, layer management, Loading data (vector, raster, CSV, shape files), Coordinate reference systems; Georeferencing Scanned Maps: Adding and managing control points, QGIS Georeferencer Plugin, Transforming raster maps; Digitization and Vector: Creating vector layer, Heads-up digitization, Editing tools, Attribute table management, length, and count calculations

units.title: Remote Sensing Data Analysis and Applications
units.topics: Image Preprocessing: Radiometric Correction, Geometric Correction, Resampling techniques; Image Classification Techniques: Unsupervised Classification (ISODATA, K-means), Supervised Classification (training sample collection, Maximum Likelihood, Minimum Distance, Accuracy assessment); NDVI, LULC, and Change Detection: NDVI formula and interpretation, LULC Mapping, Change Detection; Applications of RS and GIS: Disaster Management, Agriculture Monitoring, Urban Planning, Water resource management

units.title: Remote Sensing Data Analysis and Applications – Practical
units.topics: Image Processing and Classification in QGIS and SAGA GIS: Importing and visualizing satellite images, Layer stacking and band combination, Image enhancement, Unsupervised and Supervised classification; NDVI Calculation and Vegetation Mapping: Calculating NDVI using raster calculator, Creating NDVI-based vegetation health maps; Thematic Mapping Project: Creating a Thematic Map Using Multi-Source Spatial Data, Area of Interest, Map design elements and layout export
